spells/shadow-landscape-717.name: Shadow Landscape
spells/shadow-landscape-717.effectSummary: Transforms natural terrain throughout a one-mile-radius spread for 1 day per caster level. Desert or tundra shifts 30°F hotter or colder, respectively, and produces hourly sandstorms or snowstorms. In forests, light undergrowth becomes heavy and existing heavy undergrowth grasps creatures as entangling vegetation; in hills, light undergrowth becomes heavy, uphill movement costs 2 squares on gradual slopes or 4 on steep slopes, and cliffs require DC 25 Climb checks. In marshes, half of undergrowth spaces become quicksand. In mountains, cliffs and chasms require DC 25 Climb checks; a failed Climb check or loud noise has a 10% chance to start an avalanche; altitude exposure is treated one category worse. On natural plains, half of undergrowth spaces become entangling vegetation and thunderstorms or tornadoes are frequent. Ordinary constructed dungeons are unaffected, but natural caverns make natural-stone floor squares cost 4 squares of movement and cover 10% of floor space with stalagmites. The spell also worsens random weather: use the normal local weather table, roll twice and take the higher result, or three times on plains; do not roll random weather underground. The caster ignores the spell's terrain-specific hindrances and can designate one traveler per four caster levels to ignore them as well, though designated travelers still suffer the worsened weather. The caster can also designate native animals, plants, or magical beasts totaling up to 1 HD per caster level as shadow guardians. While a guardian stays in the area it is friendly to the caster and designated travelers and gains cold resistance 10, darkvision 60 feet, damage reduction 5/magic, evasion, and low-light vision, using a better preexisting value instead of the spell's value.
